commits.message:
Review (high): a location keeps every reason, lib keys, a self-iterable pass iterator (rich-protocol-9xcs.94u)

- render-purity reports every reason a location has, so a State in a Memo
  held by a module let is refused even when a debt row owes the let.
- TypeScript lib declarations are keyed `lib`, not by their node_modules path.
- The mobx accessor sanction names rich-protocol-9xcs.sej and says the gap.
- The pass-opening iterator sits on %IteratorPrototype%, iterable itself.
- measuring is private to protocol; scroll measures through Measurement.get.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

A render that writes state throws, and a field cannot be written (rich-protocol-9xcs.94u)

The refusal epic rich-protocol-9xcs asks for, built from the design on
rich-protocol-9xcs.rsn.

- src/core/protocol.ts owns the render phase: a pass is one outermost
  `render` or `measure` call and every step of what it returned, read
  elsewhere through `activePass()`. New `measure(measurable, options)` is
  the measure enforcer; `withBoundedWidth`, `Measurement.get` and every
  direct `.measure(` call go through it, and test/seam/render-calls gains
  the measure half.
- src/core/state.ts: `State<T>`, whose `set` throws `RenderWriteError`
  in a pass that did not make it (React's ownership line). rsn called it
  `Cell`; "cell" is this library's terminal character cell.
- test/seam/render-purity: nothing writable is reachable from a
  renderable's fields, a class's statics or module scope, but through
  `State`, `Memo` (never of a `State`) or a mobx accessor in src/widgets/.
  The 231 locations that exist today are seeded, shrink-only, in
  render-purity-debt.ts, each with what it becomes and why.

Only the iterator of the call that opens a pass is wrapped: wrapping every
level cost ~30% of render time (Table in two Panels, 11.8 vs 9.1 ms);
opener-only measures 8.9 ms.
Review: the template frames test names FrameSequence, not the removed Frames (rich-animation-27tq.0tc)

Review: the pulse test reads what Progress draws; one clock in the showcase (rich-animation-27tq.0tc)

The BarColumn pulse test supplied its own frame and compared against a
literal 7.5; it now prints the Progress and compares each row to the bar
drawn in a frame for 7.5s. A test pins that, in a frame of its own host,
a Progress holds what it would draw. Spinner's placed renderable is built
in the constructor after the sequences it closes over. The showcase draws
the dashboard at the Live's frame time, so the heading and the jobs share
one clock. Two doc sentences that described examples no longer present
are corrected.

An animation is drawn one way: placed (rich-animation-27tq.0tc)

Removes every public way to draw an animation at a time the caller names:
frameAt and its Stamped renderable, the Frames class, Spinner.drawnAt, and
ProgressBar's pulse: { t }, now pulse: true. A FrameSequence, a Spinner and a
pulse are placed and draw at the frame's time.

Progress draws its table in a frame of its own host's time when printed with
none, so the bars and spinners placed in it draw at the moment its tasks are
drawn at. Examples and docs place their animations; docs that played an effect
over frames at sampled moments now play it in a live fence.

The every-kind playground test draws at the times it checks (rich-animation-42lg.6wt) (#502)

* The every-kind playground test draws at the times it checks (rich-animation-42lg.6wt)

The test was named for three draws and made about 1,900: 32 seconds of
clock at sixty frames a second, each frame the whole 120x90 gallery.
It now plays at the playground's one-frame-a-second rate, so the half
minute is a frame a second. Locally 11.3 s -> 0.27 s; it timed out at
30 s on CI.

Two costs in the frame itself, found on the way:

- kinds.ts made every effect anew inside draw(t), so a gradient's
  legible-ink memo started cold on every frame. Each effect is now made
  once and drawn with frameAt.
- Oklch.deltaE worked out four sines and cosines per comparison; a
  colour matched against a 256-colour palette paid them per entry. Each
  colour now keeps its OKLab a and b, by the same formula.

Gallery draw at 256 colours: 3.7 -> 2.6 ms, flat from t = 0 to 10^6.

* Review: one OKLab conversion, the gallery test samples mid-phase near a million (rich-animation-42lg.6wt)

- labOf is the one polar-to-OKLab spelling; deltaE and toRgba both use it.
- The every-kind test asserts it is at 1 fps, and seeks half a second
  after a frame so the draws near 10^6 s fall mid-phase, not on whole seconds.
- kinds.ts: effected takes no identity-function mode; the border kinds use
  aroundPanel, which names the panel once.
